Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 08/12/2026
Patient: Maxwell Veum, 80-year-old male

Subjective:
Mr. Veum presents for his routine follow-up. He reports no new complaints today and feels generally well.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable and within normal limits. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Musculoskeletal exam shows no tenderness or deformity.

Assessment:
Mr. Veum is an 80-year-old male with no new issues at this visit. His overall health status remains stable.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine monitoring. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up as scheduled or sooner if any new symptoms arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/04/2026
Patient: Maxwell Veum, 80-year-old male

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/04/2026: acute osteoporotic L1 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L1 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. No other acute abnormalities are identified.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician based on clinical presentation.

notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/12/2026
Patient: Maxwell Veum, 80-year-old male

History:
Back pain began 08/09/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 5 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 6/10 despite 4 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and calcitonin nasal spray, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.

Assessment:
The patient presents with persistent and worsening back pain related to a vertebral fracture sustained after lifting a laundry basket. Conservative treatment has been followed as outlined.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and bracing. Consider interventional options if pain remains refractory.
